What?

Can you elaborate on this? Links to bugs?
This was an error I saw, then a quick googling of the error.  I can get more details together (probably tomorrow).
I added links to a couple of bugs where others have done the same thing.
Sure, but what _specifically_ is the problem? And what's being done to fix it at the source? These are work-arounds.

> Sure, but what specifically is the problem? 

Code doesn't compile and warns about mismatching enums (because they do mismatch)

Specifically, the headers are mismatched between some specific linux versions and glibc.  My understanding is that the source is already fixed, but you can't really backport the new user API headers, so the workaround seems to be to make sure that you #include headers in the right order, which is what we did before, just implicitly.  I also don't understand this fully, I just rearranged the #includes and triggered this issue.

If there's a better fix, I'm happy to do it, I just don't see what that would be.

> If there's a better fix, I'm happy to do it, I just don't see what that would be.

I'm trying to understand that and I already asked for the specifics. To clarify, I'd like to see the actual compiler error output of this specific problem, which may help me pinpoint patches that might fix it, if they exist. Not trying to be painful here, just if something's broken with the headers, it's broken for more than just dbus-sensors, and so deserves a fix that isn't a work-around specific to dbus-sensors.

Maybe it's the case that this is the best we can do in the circumstances, but it certainly isn't clear to me that it's true, yet.
And to be clear, not worried about you being difficult.  if there's a better way to fix this, I'm all ears, this is just what I could come up with.

Oh. So. Because the first header you moved was `<linux/mctp.h>` I had the impression that we'd messed something up with the kernel MCTP headers (... that I wasn't aware of), and that the links were just to similar "linux / glibc messed up, here's how we resolved it" issues.

Can you mention the specific conflicting definitions in the comment so it's clear that the links are actually directly relevant?

Ah, that makes more sense.  Yeah, no problems with mctp.h

I added the actual compiler error in the comment.
Closing this out because I think you're good with this now?  If not, please reopen.
Can we consider unifying this with `src/mctp/MctpEndpoint.[ch]pp`? Maybe promote it under `src/`?

Happy to unify if we can, but I don't really see how.  To use the asio sockets, we explicitly need something that can explicitly use

boost::asio::generic::datagram_protocol::endpoint

I'm not sure Making the exiting MCTPEndpoint inherit from that class makes sense.  Maybe we just make this asio class inherit from MCTPEndpoint?   Although I'm not sure the interfaces quite match up.

What are your thoughts?

Yeah, I understand there's a bit of a mismatch in the current needs, but I think that points to it all needing some design thought (which I haven't done). It just doesn't seem great to have two similarly named classes floating around doing completely different things.

Specifically here, what are you thinking?  I could pull the asio dependency into MctpEndpoint? (maybe through an ifdef?). That doesn't seem right.

It looks like these might be two objects with the same name but different purposes.  This one is a wrapper to reasonably get at the sockaddr_mctp in a safe way.  src/mctp/MCTPEndpoint.hpp looks like a wrapper around dbus to watch for endpoint changes.  I suspect we should just name them appropriately?

MCTPAddress for this one?
Existing could go to MCTPDBusEndpoint
and this one becomes MCTPNetEndpoint.

So my comment was more idle musing than something actionable.

However, I expect it's not worth trying to talk to an endpoint if it's not represented in the mctpd object tree. Given that instances of the classes in `src/mctp/MCTPEndpoint.[ch]pp` reflect the MCTP endpoint's lifecycle, it would seem sensible for that `MCTPEndpoint` to be able to produce one of these ASIO wrappers?

Again, just musing on an possible direction, not intending to hold anything up necessarily. Maybe fixing naming does solve the problem, though I'd more lean towards incorporating `ASIO` or `Socket` for this class, given they're fundamental to its implementation.

> So my comment was more idle musing than something actionable.
> 
> However, I expect it's not worth trying to talk to an endpoint if it's not represented in the mctpd object tree. Given that instances of the classes in `src/mctp/MCTPEndpoint.[ch]pp` reflect the MCTP endpoint's lifecycle, it would seem sensible for that `MCTPEndpoint` to be able to produce one of these ASIO wrappers?

My thought there is to not impose an asio requirement for applications that didn't otherwise need it.  I could move this into something like src/mctp/asio/x.hpp just so it's common, then at least we have something common?

> 
> Again, just musing on an possible direction, not intending to hold anything up necessarily. Maybe fixing naming does solve the problem, though I'd more lean towards incorporating `ASIO` or `Socket` for this class, given they're fundamental to its implementation.

I can rename, I think that's a good idea.

updated to do that.

I agree, a generic socket class would be a good thing.  That's where I'm hoping to get cleaning up MctpRequester:

https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/master/src/nvidia-gpu/MctpRequester.hpp

Which I'm starting to hack together here:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/84097

`MctpAsioEndpoint` now.
Fixed
This rename addresses my concern, so +1 on that front.
Can you add Tested?

The current code doesn't seem to work on the platform I have (see Marcs series), so I'm not sure how to test on this patch.  Once we get to the end of the series we can test, or if you want to cherry pick this to your platforms, maybe that works?
